subject: Question about spatial regression with categorical confounders

messages.author: f2baaf6252beabe3
messages.subject: Question about spatial regression with categorical confounders
parts:
I have a bit of a biostat 101 question that's stumping me. I'm performing spatial regression in R-INLA, and have a four-level categorical confounder (coded as 0, 1, 2, 3) that I'm adjusting for using "+ as.factor(var)", as I would with a glm model. I have no interest in interpreting the coefficient for this variable. However when I look at summary.fixed from my model output, I see there's a coefficient for each level of the confounder in question, including for level 0. This makes me unsure how to interpret the coefficient I am interested in. 

I attached a screenshot of my output (density_med is what I care about, disaster is the variable in question). 

Thanks,
Julianne

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Question about spatial regression with categorical confounders
parts:
I would guess that you have no intercept in the model, and then
a factor would expand to all levels, like

> x = as.factor(1:4); y = as.numeric(x)
> model.matrix(y ~ -1 + x, data = data.frame(x,y))
x1 x2 x3 x4
1 1 0 0 0
2 0 1 0 0
3 0 0 1 0
4 0 0 0 1
attr(,"assign")
[1] 1 1 1 1
attr(,"contrasts")
attr(,"contrasts")$x
[1] "contr.treatment"


but if you add the intercept, then the first level (by default) will be
set to zero

> model.matrix(y ~ 1 + x, data = data.frame(x,y))
(Intercept) x2 x3 x4
1 1 0 0 0
2 1 1 0 0
3 1 0 1 0
4 1 0 0 1
attr(,"assign")
[1] 0 1 1 1
attr(,"contrasts")
attr(,"contrasts")$x
[1] "contr.treatment"


there is an entry about this, at the FAQ list at r-inla.org

H
